mechanism_narrative: A quarterly increase in GDPC1 indicates strengthening economic demand, leading to increased consumer spending and, subsequently, higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of quarters with positive GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.5%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle, increasing borrowing costs and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 1.5-year rolling window during tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: Jointly, when UNRATE falls below 6% and PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 in a month, it indicates a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Triggered signals result in negative SPX returns more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in INDPRO, indicating improved industrial production, suggests increased economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, but only during non-recessionary periods.
failure_condition: SPX returns are insignificantly different from baseline during non-recessionary periods with INDPRO growth (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in HOUST, indicating housing market strength, suggests increased consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward analysis shows no significant positive correlation between HOUST growth and SPX returns over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL exceeds a 3-month average increase of 0.5%, it signals rising inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated monetary tightening.
failure_condition: Triggered signals result in positive SPX returns more than 55% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of a UNRATE below 5% and a RSAFS increase above $500,000 signals a strong economy with high consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint trigger activation does not yield significantly higher SPX returns than single-proxy triggers (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Always, GDPC1 growth rates provide a baseline indicator of economic health, with positive growth rates corresponding to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, regardless of regime.
failure_condition: Walk-forward analysis reveals a negative correlation between GDPC1 growth and SPX returns over any 3-year window.
